clue.text: Where one may fall asleep out of boredom?

indicators.note: out of suggests the letters of the next word are shaken loose and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone so bored they nod off, wondering where sleep might take them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of boredom' reads as the reason for falling asleep, but 'out of' is the anagram signal: BOREDOM rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping room is the usual place a person drops off at night.

clue.text: Home fixture-City bringing up objection

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means the word below is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: A football report: a City home fixture brings up an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home fixture' sounds like a football match at home; it is a fitting in a house. In this down entry 'bringing up' turns the objection word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub for bathing is a permanent fitting plumbed into a house.

clue.text: Very experienced fingerprint taker?

definitions.meaning: an expert, someone highly skilled at something

explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is an adept expert; literally a hand making dabs, which is slang for fingerprints.

clue.text: Where to put chalk, given the signal

definitions.meaning: snooker players chalk the tip of the stick they strike with
at exactly the prompted moment, as an actor entering at the prompt

explanation.definitionFit: Billiard chalk goes onto the playing stick, and an actor responding to a prompt arrives at the right moment.

clue.text: Hooch? Nonsense!

explanation.definitionFit: Illegally distilled liquor is the American slang sense; foolish talk is the other sense.

clue.text: He may remove people from unfriendly ball

definitions.meaning: a doorman who throws troublemakers out of a club
in cricket, a short-pitched delivery that rears up at the batsman

explanation.surface: A host evicting guests from a ball that has turned hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: A club doorman ejects rowdy guests; in cricket a fast short delivery rising toward the batter has the same name.

clue.text: Wide, for a minor way?

definitions.meaning: in Britain, ... are minor roads, below A roads

explanation.surface: Asking whether a broad path counts as a lesser route.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad means wide; read as B road it is a British minor route ranked below main roads.

clue.text: Ran United badly, having no coaching

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A football club run so poorly that its players got no coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters of RAN UNITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has never been taught or drilled lacks any training.

clue.text: Porter may transmit infection

definitions.meaning: someone who carries luggage or loads
a person or animal passing on a disease without necessarily suffering from it

explanation.surface: A railway porter who might be spreading germs.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter bears loads for others; a disease host passes infection on to others.

clue.text: Unfairly small helping of steak tartare?

definitions.text: Unfairly small helping of steak tartare?

parts.words: Unfairly small helping of steak tartare?
parts.note: steak tartare is served uncooked, so a stingy portion of it is an uncooked share, which in idiom means unfair treatment

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unjust treatment; literally an uncooked portion, as steak tartare is.

clue.text: You can put this in your pipe and smoke it

definitions.text: You can put this in your pipe and smoke it

parts.words: You can put this in your pipe and smoke it
parts.note: plays on the idiom telling someone to accept an unwelcome fact, taken literally as what fills a pipe

explanation.definitionFit: Leaf dried for smoking is what is literally packed into a pipe and lit.

clue.text: Get too big for one's boots?

definitions.text: Get too big for one's boots?

parts.words: Get too big for one's boots?
parts.note: the idiom means becoming conceited, but taken literally it is a child's feet becoming too large for their footwear

explanation.definitionFit: Children whose feet lengthen become too large for old shoes, the literal sense behind the idiom.

clue.text: Went over jazz setting for poem

indicators.note: setting is used as a jeweller sets a stone, the first word holding the second inside it

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz
a verse is a poem or piece of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone checked a jazz arrangement of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' sounds like music set to words, but it signals one piece holding the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing or moving across ground is to travel over it.

clue.text: Get older — about 49-but physically nimble

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, the first word placed round the second

parts.note: to age is to grow older
in Roman numerals IL is a (non-standard) way to write 49

explanation.surface: Someone nearing fifty who has aged yet stays fit and spry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 49' looks like an approximate age; 'about' is a container signal, and 49 is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick and light on one's feet is the bodily sense of nimble.

clue.text: Harry losing the right to distinctive emblem

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word for harry

parts.note: to badger is to harry or pester
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Prince Harry gives up his entitlement to a royal emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads as a name, but it is a verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin or crest worn to show membership or rank is a distinctive emblem.

clue.text: Clear former wife over one charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the rest

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
taken as written
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A divorcee is cleared of a charge brought against her ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts EX above ONE and RATE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to declare them blameless of an accusation.

clue.text: A popular soldier, by and large

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked soldier described as, on the whole, a good sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean usually or on the whole.

clue.text: It used to tear through rigging, and could make other gaps

definitions.text: It used to tear through rigging

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of the next words might be reshaped into another word

explanation.surface: Old naval shot ripped sails and ropes, leaving more holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusters of small iron balls fired from naval cannon shredded the enemy's sails and ropes.

clue.text: No excuse for dirt in such a programme?

definitions.text: No excuse for dirt in such a programme?

parts.words: No excuse for dirt in such a programme?
parts.note: a long-running TV drama is named after detergent sponsors, so with all that cleanser around nobody could be dirty

explanation.definitionFit: Serial TV dramas were named after the detergent makers who sponsored them.

clue.text: Meets bill for old furniture

definitions.meaning: high-backed wooden benches of a traditional kind

explanation.surface: Someone pays for some antique furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying an account clears it; old-fashioned high-backed benches share the name.

clue.text: A prize that is degenerate

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: A cup award said to be in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link word; 'degenerate' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue that wastes away through disuse is said to waste or decline in this way.

clue.text: Pulls turf back

indicators.note: back means the word for turf is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: sward is grassy turf

explanation.surface: A gardener tugs a piece of lawn back.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something along is to drag or tug it.

clue.text: Performer whose part is terrible, though not entirely

indicators.note: though not entirely says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An entertainer whose role is awful, though only partly so.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Performer whose' as the definition; 'whose' is only a link word and 'Performer' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer on stage, such as a singer or dancer, is a professional performer.

clue.text: Reservation carries little weight

definitions.meaning: an apothecaries' unit of twenty grains

explanation.surface: A doubt that counts for little.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral hesitation is a qualm; an old apothecaries' unit is a tiny weight of twenty grains.

clue.text: Brieftime with the Irish

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: A short stay among the people of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt, short speech is concise and to the point.

clue.text: Soldiers enter plane, a cargo carrier

indicators.note: enter says the soldiers go inside the word for plane

parts.note: a fighter is a combat plane
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops board an aircraft carrying cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like the cargo carrier itself, but it is the combat aircraft that the soldiers 'enter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or aircraft built to transport goods is a cargo vessel.

clue.text: Loses colour from sofa designed to keep it

indicators.note: the phrase sofa designed is said to keep, or hold, the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A sofa designed to keep its colour loses it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep it' tells you the answer is held inside SOFA DESIGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that bleaches in sunlight grows paler and pales away.

clue.text: Gone out to get a rich cake

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word before it are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes out for a rich cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GONE, then A is added. GENOA cake is a British rich fruit cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A Genoa is a rich fruit cake with almonds, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Boy conceals scheme to see part of Scandinavia

indicators.note: conceals says the word for boy hides the word for scheme inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A boy hides his plan to visit the Arctic north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' signals the boy word holding the scheme word; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami region across arctic Norway, Sweden and Finland lies in Scandinavia.

clue.text: Command to surrender and push off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of the words before it have gone wrong and are reordered

explanation.surface: An order to give up, followed by a shove to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'push off' reads as go away, but 'off' signals an anagram of AND PUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the arms is what a gunman orders captives to do in yielding.

clue.text: Reluctance to throw at head

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring capes

explanation.surface: Unwilling to throw something at someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland here, NESS as in place names like Sheerness. 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity in company shows itself as reluctance to come forward.

clue.text: The bar is swinging

parts.note: sounds like a lively pub, but describes a horizontal pole hung on ropes in a circus

explanation.definitionFit: A circus acrobat's horizontal pole hangs on two ropes and swings.
